Favorite thing I’ve read so far this year: Janet Malcolm’s “In The Freud Archives”

Favorite things I read in 2025: Elena Ferrante’s “My Brilliant Friend” and Marguerite Yourcenar’s “Memoirs of Hadrian”
No matter how well-known Arkady Martine's "A Memory Called Empire" is, it deserves more.
Saw an AI bro refer to "brain-only writers" lol
(Turns out a tobacco settlement is a fixed cost that affects neither demand elasticity nor marginal cost, so you should just keep selling cheap cigs to maximize revenue)

I bought a managerial economics textbook for some self-guided learning, it’s been a handy guide to “here’s why everything feels like ass.” 

quiz question on how to precisely maximize profits after your cigarette company has a tobacco settlement
half the stuff I read about political media these days is like “hey man, if you’re not at the fart factory with the Fart King no one’s gonna smell your farts”
Fighting over Bluesky and X is so funny. It's like two rival opera companies screaming at each other.  Persuasion is done via short form video now, we're both retirement homes for uggos.
yes! bsky.app/profile/will...
mattdpearce.substack.com/p/you-couldn...
there were two barbers, one with a good haircut and one with a bad haircut, and I chose the one that used AI
the single most important thing for the survival of the galactic spaceship is a magazine of ideas
What so many have experienced personally has been confirmed by a new study: AI has been a disaster for working artists.

"The loss of local media in particular is associated with greater loneliness, lower awareness of public officials, and more corruption. It’s like an invisible tax levied on our communities.... Increasingly, this invisible tax is being silently levied by Big Tech."
Thank you my friend!

I think about this a lot. I talk to non-journos who give me half-surfaced versions of current events, and it’s hard for good info to find them. And they’re relatively high-functioning professionals! If navigating the info economy is hard for them, how does it work for people with fewer advantages?

I wrote about being inundated with AI writing at every turn, unwittingly turning my brain into the AI police, and how shitty AI writing is randomly showing up in my real life outside of the internet
